papers.title: Machine learning based recommendation of agricultural and horticultural crop farming in India under the regime of NPK, soil pH and three climatic variables
papers.dataset: Kaggle crop set (paper: 2,100 points, 11 agricultural + 10 horticultural crops; N, P, K, pH, rainfall, temperature, humidity)
papers.method: XGBoost, SVM, RF, KNN, DT; separate models for agricultural, horticultural and combined crops
papers.method_quote: the learning rate was set to 0.1, max depth to 17, n estimators to 200, subsample rate was set to 0.5, gamma value was set to 0, and the seed was set to 50 (Sec 2.2.2)
papers.metric_quote: XGBoost demonstrated the highest test accuracy of 99.09 % and KNN demonstrated the lowest test accuracy of 94.45 % for agricultural crops. (Sec 3.2, Table 1)
papers.protocol: single random 70/30 split; under-sampling (order vs split not stated)
papers.protocol_quote: The training dataset consisted of 70 % of the available data, while the remaining 30 % was reserved for testing purposes. (Sec 2.3)
papers.availability: Data will be made available on request.
papers.gap_text: One random split of the Kaggle table with no location or year, so 99% says nothing about a new state. What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

methods.name: Persistence
methods.note: repeats the district's last-year yield ranking; needs history for every crop

methods.name: LightGBM pointwise
methods.note: same pairs and features as YieldRank, squared-error loss on yield percentile

methods.name: YieldRank (ours)
methods.note: LightGBM LambdaMART on (district-season, crop) pairs, relevance = yield percentile

ablation.name: YieldRank (full)
ablation.note: history + yield target + listwise/pointwise blend + persistence term + conformal sets

ablation.name: YieldRank - yield target (area share)
ablation.note: relevance = current area share (what is grown most) instead of yield percentile

ablation.name: LightGBM pointwise
ablation.note: pointwise regression on yield percentile alone

ablation.name: YieldRank top-1 only
ablation.note: a single recommendation is right only Hit@1 of the time and carries no coverage guarantee

ablation.name: YieldRank fixed top-3
ablation.note: fixed-size list: coverage is whatever Hit@3 happens to be; sets do not adapt to hard cases

why: On unseen states YieldRank picks the best-yielding crop 56.3% of the time vs 38.3% for the best classifier from the literature (MLP), +18.0 points (p<10^-300).
Random splits hide this: that classifier scores 53.7% on a random split, 15.4 points more than on unseen states; YieldRank loses 3.7.
Yield grounding is the key ingredient: the same ranker trained to reproduce what farmers grow (area share) gets only 23.2% on unseen states.
District history matters: without it YieldRank falls to 27.4%.
Persistence (repeat last year's ranking) is close overall (54.4% vs 56.3%, p=8.7e-20) but cannot rank crops without last-year history: on those cold-start cases YieldRank gets 47.4% vs 42.4%.

Every single objective on the same pairs (LightGBM pointwise, LightGBM XE-NDCG ranker, XGBoost LambdaMART, LambdaMART (v4 listwise)) is below the final blend on unseen states, by at most 1.3 points: the pair formulation does most of the work, and the blend (chosen on validation, not test) adds the rest.

With the same i.i.d. calibration its 90% sets cover 87.7% on unseen states with 2.69 crops, vs 75.1% with 3.07 crops for MLP; the served state-robust sets cover 94.2% with 3.66 crops (worst state 84.5%).
It is cheap: 23 s to train and 0.228 ms per query, with tree feature importances/SHAP for explanations.

related_work_ours.note: Real Government APY data (not Kaggle); leave-states-out and leave-years-out splits; best-yielding crop as target; 90% conformal sets; paired Wilcoxon tests; no leakage (history uses strictly earlier years, state_group grouping); code in experiments/. Caveat: one country (India), no field trial.
